title: Jamie Dimon Says AI Will Eliminate Jobs, 'It Is What It Is' — But Warns Cutting $150,000 Truck Driving Jobs To $25K A Year Would Bring 'Civil Unrest'
source_used: Benzinga piece read on Yahoo Finance copy (page says 'originally appeared on Benzinga.com')
key_facts: Jamie Dimon, chief executive of JPMorgan Chase, spoke at the World Economic Forum annual meeting in Davos in January 2026 (the article says 'in January').
He said AI will eliminate some jobs, change others and probably add some, and that the speed of the change could matter as much as the technology.
He called for retraining, relocation help and income assistance, and said the US Trade Adjustment Assistance programme 'did not work'.
His truck-driver example was hypothetical: 2 million US commercial truck drivers at about $150,000 a year, moving to jobs that might pay about $25,000.
He said JPMorgan will not cut its workforce overnight but acknowledged there could be fewer employees in five years.
The page is full of sponsored financial product offers, which were ignored.
quote_evidence: "It is what it is. We're going to deploy it. Will it eliminate jobs? Yes. Will it change jobs? Yes. Will it add some jobs? Probably."
The $150,000 and $25,000 figures were hypothetical examples Dimon used to illustrate the potential economic shock of a rapid transition.
why_it_matters_hint: A bank chief's view that AI job change must be phased in to avoid unrest, grounded in his own hypothetical.
notes: OLD EVENT RE-DATED: the remarks were made at Davos in January, and the Benzinga/Yahoo piece is dated 7 Oct with no new facts.
